pitch.pitch: Shipwrecked on a volcanic island, you build a steam-and-aether frontier town, keep its people alive and decide which of four factions inherits the Cinder Spire.
pitch.playerFantasy: Be the castaway engineer who turns a wreck into a living town: half survivor, half governor, with a toolbelt and a spellbook.
pitch.mainActivity: Gather and craft by hand early, then design production chains and supply routes that feed townspeople with real needs; explore biomes guarded by bosses; trade and negotiate with factions.

references.genres: Survival-crafting, colony / town management, light action RPG.
references.referencesTaken: Hands-on survival crafting; production-chain management; faction reputation that changes prices and access.
references.referencesDifferent: Townspeople are named people with needs and routines, not worker counters; magic is an input to industry, not a separate combat school only.

audience.audience: PC players aged 18–40 who enjoy survival-crafting and want more management depth; sessions of 45–120 minutes; comfortable with menus and spreadsheets-lite UIs.

usps.name: Magic powers the machines
usps.description: Every production chain can be boosted by a magical input.
usps.playerBenefit: Optimizing feels like discovery, not just arithmetic.
usps.differentiator: Factory games have no magic; fantasy games have no production chains.

usps.name: A town that reacts to your choices
usps.description: Townspeople answer to what you build and supply.
usps.differentiator: Reference games show the effect in numbers, not in people.

pillars.name: Industry meets magic
pillars.rationale: The contrast between steam-age machinery and old magic is what makes the world distinct.
pillars.decisionTest: If a feature could exist in a plain factory game or a plain fantasy game, it needs a hook that uses both.
pillars.example: A boiler that runs faster when fed mana crystals.
pillars.nonExample: A generic conveyor belt with no magical twist.

pillars.name: Meaningful logistics
pillars.rationale: Moving goods between people and buildings is the main source of decisions.
pillars.decisionTest: If a feature adds busywork without a meaningful choice, cut it.
pillars.example: Choosing which road to upgrade when two districts starve.
pillars.nonExample: Clicking every cart by hand to start a delivery.

pillars.name: A town that feels alive
pillars.rationale: Players should care about the people they supply, not just the numbers.
pillars.decisionTest: A system must show up in what townspeople say, need or do, or it stays out of the first release.
pillars.example: A baker who leaves town when bread runs short.
pillars.nonExample: A hidden multiplier no one can see or react to.

tone.tone: Warm but weathered: brass, soot and lantern light against a strange, glowing island. Humour in the townspeople, dread near the Spire.

scope.name: Core production loop
scope.mvpRationale: Without it there is nothing to test.
scope.acceptance: A player can produce, move and consume one resource end to end.

scope.name: Townspeople with needs
scope.mvpRationale: Gives the numbers a human reason.
scope.acceptance: Unmet needs change what a townsperson does.

scope.name: Save and load
scope.mvpRationale: Needed for any play session longer than a few minutes.
scope.acceptance: A saved town loads with identical state.

scope.name: Second faction
scope.mvpRationale: The first faction proves the loop; more can follow.

scope.name: Multiplayer
scope.mvpRationale: Too large for the first release.

platform.platform: PC (Steam) first, Steam Deck verified at launch; keyboard & mouse and gamepad. Consoles considered after 1.0.

monetization.monetization: Premium, one-time purchase (24.99 EUR). Optional cosmetic supporter pack; no microtransactions affecting balance. One paid expansion planned after 1.0.

rewardsProgression.rewardsProgression: Short loops pay out materials and XP; medium loops unlock buildings and townspeople; long loops open biomes, faction perks and the Spire. Every reward feeds the next loop up: a better axe speeds gathering, a sawmill frees the player to explore, a faction alliance opens a new biome.

principles.principles: Difficulty changes pressure (needs, enemies, prices), never information. Medium is the tuned baseline; Easy forgives mistakes, Hard punishes slow planning.

presets.name: Easy
presets.intent: Relaxed: mistakes are forgiven and the town and story stay in focus.
presets.targetPlayer: Newcomers to survival and management games.

presets.name: Medium
presets.intent: The intended experience: steady pressure that rewards planning.

presets.name: Hard
presets.intent: Punishing: scarce resources and dangerous nights; every decision counts.
presets.targetPlayer: Experienced players looking for a challenge.

custom.name: Hunger speed
custom.pressure: How fast hunger and thirst drop

switching.switching: Can be lowered at any time from the pause menu; raising it only between days.
switching.timing: Takes effect at the next dawn.
switching.achievements: Achievements count on any level; a “Hard from start” badge needs Hard for the whole run.
switching.permadeath: Optional “Ironman” toggle on any level; one save slot, no reload.

storage.storage: DifficultyProfile ScriptableObject per level, overridable by the custom sliders; saved as the preset id plus slider values.

overview.model: Each faction tracks the player’s standing and its standing with every other faction (matrix). Actions shift standing with spillover to allies and rivals.
overview.decay: 1 point per week toward 0 when no action
overview.changeRules: Quests +10…+25, gifts +5, attacking members -30, trading +1 per 100 crowns spent.

questions.name: Do NPCs age and die? How is the population replenished?

extensionPoints.how: Write a quest graph asset; steps call registered actions.

classes.name: IDamageable
classes.responsibility: Anything that can be hurt: players, townspeople, creatures, buildings.

classes.name: NeedChangedEvent
classes.responsibility: Raised when a townsperson need crosses a threshold; the HUD and the town ledger listen.

classes.name: Health
classes.responsibility: Hit points, regeneration and death for the player and creatures.

classes.name: PlayerController
classes.responsibility: Movement, interaction and the inventory of the castaway.

classes.name: NpcBrain
classes.responsibility: Decays needs each simulation tick and picks the next job or errand.

classes.name: TownLedger
classes.responsibility: Stockpile and treasury of the colony.

classes.name: HealthBar
classes.responsibility: Shows the player health on the HUD.

standards.principles: Readable over clever; small classes; no singletons outside Core services; every rule here is enforced by a tool where possible.

naming.name: Textures
naming.notes: Suffix: D diffuse, N normal, M mask, E emission.

style.analyzers: Roslyn analyzers + .editorconfig in CI; warnings as errors in Core.
style.notes: Rider and VS share the same .editorconfig.

folders.name: _Project
folders.purpose: Everything the team makes. The underscore keeps it on top.

folders.name: Scripts
folders.purpose: C# code, one sub-folder per assembly.

folders.name: Core.Events
folders.purpose: Typed event bus and ScriptableObject channels.

folders.name: Core.Data
folders.purpose: Loads and validates data assets; id registry.

folders.name: Prefabs
folders.purpose: Mirrors the gameplay areas: Buildings, Npcs, Items.

folders.name: Plugins
folders.purpose: Third-party packages that are not in the Package Manager.

assetRules.name: Variants, not copies
assetRules.rule: Make a prefab variant when only values change; never duplicate a prefab.

assetRules.name: Small nested prefabs
assetRules.rule: Split big prefabs so two people rarely edit the same file.

assetRules.name: One scene per discipline
assetRules.rule: Level art, lighting and gameplay live in separate additive scenes.

assetRules.name: Data in ScriptableObjects
assetRules.rule: Tunable numbers live in SO assets, not in scene objects.

assetRules.name: Lock binary art
assetRules.rule: Lock .psd files before editing; they cannot be merged.

branches.name: task
branches.notes: Merge within two days; hide unfinished work behind a flag.

git.prRules: One task per PR, under 400 changed lines where possible, one approval, CI green.
git.notes: Binary art is locked before editing.

review.name: No missing references in changed prefabs
Dependencies only point down a layer
review.description: Check new using directives against the Technical Architecture layers.

review.name: No allocations in Update loops
review.description: No LINQ, string building or new lists per frame.

review.name: No secrets or keys in the change

principle.principle: Designers change content without code: every item, building, need, recipe, enemy and quest is a data asset with a stable id.

formats.name: ScriptableObject
formats.whenToUse: Content designers edit in Unity with references to sprites and prefabs.

formats.name: JSON
formats.whenToUse: Nested data that mods or tools must read and write.

formats.name: CSV
formats.whenToUse: Flat tables balanced in a spreadsheet: prices, stats, drop rates.

ids.stability: IDs never change after release; renames only change display names.
ids.notes: Prefix by schema (item., bld., need., rcp., enemy., quest.).

modding.loadOrder: Base game, then mods alphabetically; later definitions override by id.
modding.notes: JSON and CSV only; no scripts at 1.0.

save.requirements: Save anywhere outside combat; 3 manual slots + 3 rotating autosaves; Steam Cloud.
save.format: Compressed JSON per system, one file per save; ids not references.
save.versioning: Save version number with ordered migrations; old saves always load.
save.autosave: At every dawn and before entering a boss arena.
save.performance: Under 200 ms on the target PC; written on a background thread.

approach.approach: Utility AI for townspeople, behaviour trees for enemies, simple supply/demand rules for prices.
approach.navigation: Unity NavMesh with off-mesh links for ladders; flow fields for swarms.
approach.npc: Needs and jobs scored every in-game hour (see NPC behaviour).
approach.enemy: Patrol → chase → attack → flee; bosses scripted by phase.
approach.economy: Prices drift toward demand every tick, clamped by price rules.
approach.debug: In-game overlay shows each NPC’s top three scores.

techniques.techniques: GPU instancing for foliage, LODs, Burst-compiled simulation jobs, pooled projectiles, far-base simulation at a lower rate.
techniques.profiling: Unity Profiler and Memory Profiler weekly on the Deck; performance tests in CI on a fixed save.

bottlenecks.name: Pathfinding spikes at dusk
bottlenecks.description: All townspeople path home at once.

bottlenecks.name: Foliage overdraw in Thornwood
bottlenecks.description: Dense thickets cost 4 ms on the Deck.

env.environment: Unity 6 LTS, Rider, Git + LFS on GitHub.
env.tools: Custom item and quest inspectors; save-file viewer; debug console.
env.build: GitHub Actions + GameCI: build on every merge to main, nightly Steam branch upload.
env.logging: Structured logs with categories; crash reports via Backtrace.

items.text: Install Unity Hub and Unity 6 LTS
Install Git LFS and run git lfs install
Open the project and let the Library import
Crash reporting key in build settings

adrs.name: Use Unity 6 LTS with URP
adrs.consequences: Proven Deck performance; license cost accepted.

adrs.name: Content as ScriptableObjects with string ids
adrs.context: Designers must add content without code; saves must survive renames.
adrs.decision: ScriptableObjects in the editor, exported to JSON for mods; ids are strings.
adrs.consequences: Need an id validator in CI.

adrs.name: Simulation on a fixed tick
adrs.decision: Fixed 1 s tick with interpolation for visuals.

style.style: Stylised low-poly with painted textures; brass, soot and glowing teal aether.
style.characters: Chunky proportions, readable silhouettes by profession.
style.contrast: Warm town lights against cool, desaturated wilderness; aether is the only saturated teal.
style.ui: Parchment and brass frames, flat icons.
style.vfx: Soft particles; aether trails; corruption as inky smoke.

palettes.name: Iron Crown
palettes.notes: Navy and steel with gold trim.

mood.mood: Folk instruments with mechanical percussion; calm in town, tense near the Spire.
mood.mixing: Ducking under dialogue; separate music, SFX, ambience and voice sliders.
mood.voice: Main cast voiced, townspeople barks only.

music.name: Night watch
music.notes: Low drones; rises when monsters are near.

workflow.workflow: Concept → blockout → model → texture → review → integrate; every asset tracked below.
workflow.naming: Follows the coding asset prefixes (PF_, SO_, M_, T_).

milestones.name: M1 – Grey-box prototype
milestones.goal: Gather → craft → supply one need, end to end.

acceptance.text: One resource produced, moved and consumed

milestones.name: M2 – Vertical slice
milestones.goal: Greenhollow, Oakham and the Iron Crown in final quality.

rules.rules: P0 blocks the next milestone; estimates in ideal days; nothing enters Ready without acceptance criteria.

risks.name: Scope creep in the town simulation
risks.mitigation: Protect pillars; apply the cut order when velocity drops.

risks.name: Aether art style not readable at night
risks.mitigation: Night-lighting test scene reviewed every sprint.

method.method: Two-week sprints with a playtest every sprint end.
method.communication: Daily async stand-up in chat; Monday planning call.
method.docs: This planner is the source of truth; exported Markdown lives in the repo.

strategy.strategy: Automate the simulation, play-test the feel.
strategy.automated: Edit-mode tests for formulas and data validators; play-mode tests for a 30-day town soak on a fixed seed.
strategy.manual: Checklist pass per milestone; exploratory sessions per biome.
strategy.compat: Windows 10/11, Steam Deck, two GPU vendors.
strategy.soak: 8-hour unattended town run before each gate.

cases.name: Supply route delivers cargo
cases.steps: Create the Frontier supply route; wait one day.

cases.name: Save during night raid
cases.expected: Save is refused with a message.

cases.name: Old Boar phase transitions
cases.expected: Phase banners appear at each threshold.

goals.goals: Act 1 in about 4 hours; first winter survivable on Medium with a two-farm town; no single money source above 50 % of income.
goals.playtest: Five external testers per milestone, telemetry on deaths, starvation and money.

bugs.name: Townspeople walk through the sawmill
bugs.steps: Build a sawmill next to a house; watch at dusk.

bugs.name: Boss phase banner shows twice
bugs.steps: Hit the Old Boar with a crit across 60 %.

specs.name: Supply routes
specs.goal: Let the player move stock between bases without carrying it.
stories: As a player I want the outpost to receive food every day so I can stay out exploring.
specs.rules: A wagon carries up to its capacity; cargo leaves only above the source’s minimum stock.
specs.data: Route: from, to, cargo, quantity, frequency, travel time, risk.
specs.ui: Route list in Town overview; arrows on the map.
specs.difficulty: Raid risk scales with the Enemy strength slider.
specs.edgeCases: Destination full: cargo returns. Base destroyed: route pauses.
specs.tests: Edit-mode test for route ticks; soak test with 5 routes.

salvage.name: Wreck of the Gilded Gull
salvage.notes: The player’s own ship; tutorial salvage.
